And they blessed Rebecca, & sayd vnto hyr: Thou art oure syster growe into thousande thousandes, and thy seed possesse the gates of theyr enemies.
And Rebecca arose & hir damsels, & sat them vp vpon the camels, & went theyr way after the man. And the seruaunt toke Rebecca, & went his way.
And Isaac was a commynge from the wel of the lyuynge & seynge, for he dwelt in the south contrey,
& was gone out to walke in his meditations before the euen tide. And he lift vp his eyes & loked, and beholde the camels were comming.
And Rebecca lyft vp hir eyes & when she sawe Isaac, she lighted of the camel,
& sayd vnto the seruaunt: what man is this that cometh against vs in the feld? And the seruaunt sayd: it is my master. And then she toke hyr mantil, & put it about hyr.
And the seruaunt tolde Isaac all that he had done.
Then Isaac broughte hir into hys mother Saras tente, and toke Rebecca, and she became hys wyfe. & he loued hir: & so was Isaac comforted ouer hys mother.
25: Abraham toke hym an other wife called Ketura,
whyche bare hym Simran, Iecksan, Medan Midian, Iesback and Suah.
And Iecksan begat Seba & Dedan. And the sons of Dedan were Assurim, Letusim & Leumim.
And the sonns of Midian were Epha, Epher, Hanoch, Abida & Clda. All these were the children of Ketura.
But Abraham gaue all that he had vnto Isaac.
And vnto the sonnes of hys concubynes he gaue gyftes, and sent them away from Isaac hys sonne (whyle he yet lyued) eastwarde vnto the east contrye.
These are the dayes of the life of Abraham which he liued: an hundred & .lxxv. yere,
and then fell sycke & dyed in a lusty age (when he had liued inough) & was put vnto his people.
And hys sonnes Isaac & Ismael buried hym in the double caue in the felde of Ephron sonne of Zoar the Hethite before Mamre.
Which field Abraham bought of the sonnes of Heth: There was Abraham buried & Sara hys wyfe.
And after the death of Abraham God blessed Isaac hys sonne, whych dwelled by the well of lyuynge and seynge.
These are the generations of Ismael Abrahams sonne, whych Hagar the Egyptian Saras handmaide bare vnto Abraham.
And these are the names of the sonnes of Ismael, with theyr names in theyr kynreddes. The eldest sonne of Ismael Neuaioth, then Cedar, Adbeel, Mibsam,
Misma, Duma, Masa,
Hadar, Thema Ietur Naphis & Kedma:
These are the sonnes of Ismael, & these are their names, in their townes & castels .xij. princes of nations.
And these are the yeres of the life of Ismael, an hundred & .xxxvij. yere, & then he fel sycke & died, & was laied vnto his people.
And he dwelte from Euila to Sur that is before Egypte, as men go towarde the Assirians. And he dyed in the presence of all hys brethren.
And these are the generations of Isaac, Abrahams sonne: Abraham begat Isaac.
And Isaac was .xl. yere old when he toke Rebecca to wyfe, the doughter of Bethuel the Sirian of Mesopotamia & sister to Laban the Sirien.
And Isaac made intercession vnto the Lord for his wife, bicause she was barren: and the Lord was entreated of hym, & Rebecca hys wyfe conceyued:
& the chyldren stroue togyther wythin hir. Then she sayed: if it should go so to pas, what helpeth it that I am with chylde? And she went & axed the Lorde.

And the Lorde sayed vnto hyr: there are two maner of people in thy wombe, & two nations shall spryng out of thy bowels, and the one nation shal be mightyer then the other, & the eldest shalbe seruant vnto the yonger.
And when hir tyme was come to be deliuered: behold there were two twynes in hir wombe.
And he that came out fyrst was redde & rough ouer al as it were an hyde: and they called hys name Esau.
And afterward hys brother came out, & his hand holding Esau by the hele. Wherefore his name was called Iacob. And Isaac was .lx. yere old when she bare them:
& the boyes grewe, & Esau became a conynge hunter, and a tyl man. But Iacob was a simple man, & dwelled in the tentes
Isaac loued Esau bicause he dyd eate of his venison, but Rebecca loued Iacob.
Iacob sod potage, & Esau came from the feld and was fainety,
& sayd to Iacob: let me sup of the redde potage, for I am faynty. And therfore was his name called Edom.
And Iacob sayd: sell me thys day thy byrthryght.
And Esau answered: Lo, I am at the poynte to dye, & what profit shall this byrthryghte do me?
And Iacob said swere to to me then this day. And he swore to him, & solde hys byrthryght vnto Iacob.
Then Iacob gaue Esau bread & potage of redde ryse. And he eat and dronke & rose vp, & wente hys waye. And so Esau regarded not hys byrthryght.
26: And there fel a derth in the land passyng the fyrst derth that fell in the dayes of Abraham. Wherfore Isaac wente vnto Abimelech kynge of the Phylystyans vnto Gerar.
Then the Lord appeared vnto hym and sayed: Go not downe into Egypte but hyde in the lande whych I say vnto the:
soiourne in thys lande, and I wyll be wyth the, and wyll blesse the: for vnto the, and vnto thy seed, I wil giue al these contryes. And I wyl perfourme the oth which I sware vnto Abraham thy father,
& wyl multiply thy sede as the stars of heauen, & will gyue vnto thy sede al these contries. And thorow thi sede shal all the nacions of the earth be blessed,
because that Abraham herkened vnto my voyce, & kepe myne ordinaunces, commaundementes, statutes and lawes.
And Isaac dwelled in Gerar.

And the men of the place asked him of his wife, & he said that she was hys sister: for he feared to call hyr his wyfe, lest the men of the place shold haue killed him for hir sake, bicause she was beutiful to the eye.
And it happened after he had bene there long tyme, that Abimelech kynge of the Philistians loked out at a wyndow, & sawe Isaac sportyng wt Rebecca hys wife.

And Abimelech sente for Isaac, & sayed: see, she is of a suretye thy wyfe, & why saydest thou that she was thy sister? And Isaac said vnto hym: I thought that I myght peraduenture haue dyed for her sake.
Then sayd Abimelech: why haste thou done this vnto vs? one of the people myghte lyghtlye haue lyne by thy wife, and so shuldest thou haue brought synne vpon vs.
Than Abimelech charged all his people, saying: he that toucheth this man or his wyfe, shall suerlie dye for it.
And Isaac sowed in that lande, & found in that same yere an .C. bushels: for the Lorde blessed hym,
& the man waxed myghty, and went forth and grewe tyll he was exceading greate,
that he had possession of shepe, of oxen, and a mighty housholde: so that the Philistians had enuye at hym:
in so muche that they stopped and filled vp wyth earth al the welles whyche hys fathers seruantes digged in hys father Abrahams tyme.
Then sayed Abimelech vnto Isaac: gett the from me, for thou art myghtier then we a great deale.
Then Isaac departed thence, & pitched his tente in the valey Gerar, & dwelt there.

And Isaac digged againe the welles of water which they digged in the dayes of Abraham his father, which the Philistians had stopped after the death of Abraham, & gaue them the same nams which his father gaue them.
As Isaacs seruauntes digged in the valay, they found a wel of liuing water,
And the herdmen of Gerar did stryue with Isaacs herdmen, saying: the water is ours. Then called he the well Eseck, bicause they stroue with him.
Then digged they an other well, & they stroue for that also. Therfore called he it Sitena.
And then he departed thence, & digged another wel for that which they stroue not: therfore called he it Rehoboth, saying: the Lorde hath now made vs rowme, & we ar encreased vpon the earth.
Afterwarde departed he thence and came to Bersaba.
And the Lorde appeared vnto hym the same nyght, & sayd: I am the God of Abraham thy father, feare not for I am wyth the, and wyll blesse the, and multiply thy sede for my seruaunt Abrahams sake.
And then he builded an aultare there, and called vpon the name of the Lord, and there pitched hys tent. And ther Isaacs seruauntes digged a well.
Then came Abimelech to hym from Gerar & Ahusath his frende and Phitol hys chyefe captayne.
And Isaac sayd vnto them: wherfore come ye to me, seyng ye hate me & haue put me away from you?
Then sayed they: we sawe that the Lorde was wyth the, & therfore we sayed that there should be an oothe betwexte vs & the, & that we woulde make a bond wyth the,
that thou shouldest do vs no hurt, as we haue not touched the, and haue done vnto the nothynge but good, & sent the away in peace: for thou art nowe the blessed of the Lorde.
And he made them a feast, and they ate & dronke.
And they rose vp by tymes in the morninge, and sware one to an other, And Isaac sent them away. And they departed from hym in peace.
And that same daye came Isaacs seruauntes, & told hym of a well whych they had dygged: and said vnto him, that they had found water.
And he called it Seba, wherfore the name of the cyty is called Berseba vnto thys daye.
When Esau was .xl. yere old, he toke to wyfe Iudith the doughter of Bery an Hethyte, & Basmath the doughter of Elou an Hethite,
also whyche were disobedient vnto Isaac and Rebecca.
27: And it came to passe that Isaac wexed olde and hys eyes were dymme, so that he coulde not see. Then called he Esau his eldest sonne & sayed vnto him: my sonne. And he sayd vnto hym: here am I.
And he sayed: beholde, I am old, & know not the day of my death:
now therfore take thy weapens, thy quiuer & thy bowe, & gette the to the fyeldes, and take me some venison,
and make me meate suche as I loue, and brynge it me, and let me eat that my soule may blesse the before that I dye.
But Rebecca hearde when Isaac spake to Esau hys sonne. And as sone as Esau was gone to the fielde to catche venyson, and to bryng it,
she spake to Iacob hir sonne saying? Beholde I haue heard thy father talking with Esau thy brother & saying:
bringe me venyson & make me meate that I may eate and blesse the before the Lord yer I dye.
Now therfore my sonne heare my voice in that whiche I commaunde the:
gette the to the flocke, & bryng me thence two good kyddes, and I wyll make meate of them for thy father, such as he loueth.
And thou shalt brynge it to thy father, & he shall eate, that he may blesse the before hys death.
Then said Iacob to Rebecca his mother: beholde, Esau my brother is rough, & I am smooth.
My father shall peraduenture fele me, & I shal seme vnto him as though I went about to begyle hym, & so shall he brynge a cursse vpon me, & not a blessing:
& his mother sayd vnto hym: Vpon me be thy cursse my sonne, onely heare my voyce, & go & fetch me them.
And Iacob went & fet them, & brought them to his mother. And his mother made meat of them, accordyng as hys father loued.
And she went and fet goodlye raymente of hir eldest sonne Esau, which she had in the house with hir, and put theym vpon Iacob hir yongest sonne,
and she putte the skynnes vpon hys handes, and vpon the smooth of hys necke.
And she putt the meate and breade whyche she had made in the handes of hyr son Iacob.
And he went in to his father saying: my father. And he answered: here am I: who arte thou my sonne?
And Iacob said vnto his father: I am Esau thi eldest sonne, I haue done according as thou baddest me: vp & sit, & eat of my venison, that thy soule may blesse me.
But Isaac sayd vnto his sonne: how commeth it that thou hast found it so quickely my sonne? He answered. The Lord thi God brought it to my hande.
Then sayd Isaac vnto Iacob: come nere and let me fele the mi sonne, whether thou be my sonne Esau or not.
Then went Iacob to Isaac his father, and he felt him & said: the voice is Iacobs voice, but the handes are the handes of Esau.
And he knewe hym not, bicause hys handes were rough as his brother Esaus handes: & so he blessed hym.
And he axed him: art thou my sonne Esau? And he said that I am.
Then said he: brynge me & let me eate of my sonnes venison, that my soule mai blesse the. And he brought him & he ate. And he brought him wine also, & he dranke.
And his father Isaac saied vnto hym: come nere, & kisse me my sonne.
And he wente vnto him and kissed him. And he smelled the sauour of hys rayment, & blessed hym, and sayd: Se, the smel of my sonne is as the smell of a fyld which the Lorde hath blessed.
God giue the he dewe of heauen, & of the fatnes of the earth, & plenty of corne & wine.
People be thy seruauntes, & nations bowe vnto the. Be Lord ouer thy brethren, & thy mothers chyldren stoupe vnto the. Curssed be he that curseth the, & blessed be he that blesseth the.
As sone as Isaac had made an ende of blesinge, Iacob was scace gone out from the presence of Isaac his father: then came Esau his brother from his huntynge,
& had made also meate, & brought it vnto hys father, & sayed vnto hym. Aryse my father, and eate of thy sonnes venison, that thy soule may blesse me.
Then his father Isaac saied vnto him: who art thou? he answered: I am thy eldest sonne Esau.

And Isaac was greatly astonied oute of measure, & sayed. Where is he then that hath hunted venison and brought it me, & I haue eaten of all before thou camest, & haue blessed hym, & he shall be blessed styll.
When Esau herd the wordes of hys father, he cryed out greatly & bytterly aboue measure, & said vnto his father: blesse me also mi father.
And he sayd: thy brother came wyth subtilty, & hath taken away thy blessinge.

Then sayed he: He maye well be called Iacob, for he hath vndermined me now two tymes, fyrste he toke away my byrthryght: & se, nowe hathe he taken away my blessynge also. And he sayed, hast thou kept neuer a blessyng for me?

Isaac answered and saied vnto Esau: behold I haue made hym thy Lord, and al his mothers children haue I made his seruantes. Moreouer with corne & wyne haue I stablyshed him, what can I do vnto the now my sonne?
And Esau sayd vnto his father: haste thou but the one blessing my father? blesse me also my father: so lifted vp Esau hys voyce and wept.
Then Isaac his father answered & sayd vnto him: behold thy dwellyng place shall haue of the fatnes of the earth, and of the dewe of heauen from aboue.
And with thy swerd shalt thou liue, & shalt be thy brothers seruaunt. But the time wil come, when thou shalt get the mastry, & louse hys yocke from of thy necke.
And Esau hated Iacob, bicause of the blessyng that hys father blessed hym with all, & sayed in hys hert. The dayes of my fathers sorowes are at hand, for I wyll slea my brother Iacob.
And these wordes of Esau hyr eldest sonne were tolde to Rebecca. And she sent & called Iacob hyr yongest sonne, & said vnto him: beholde thy brother Esau threateneth to kyll the:
now therfore my sonne hear my voyce, make the redy, & fle to Laban my brother at Haran:
& tary wyth hym a whyle vntil thy brothers fearcnes be swaged,
& vntyl thy brothers wrath turne away from the and he forget that whiche thou hast done to hym. Then wyl I send & fet the away from thence. Why should I losse you boeth in one daye.

And Rebecca spake to Isaac: I am werye of my life, for feare of the doughters of Heth. If Iacob take a wife of the doughters of Heth, such one as these are, or of the daughters of the land, what lust shold I haue to lyue.
28: Then Isaac called Iacob hys sonne and blessed hym, and charged hym, and sayed vnto hym: se thou take not a wyfe of the daughters of Canaan,
but aryse and gette the to Mesapotamia to the house of Bethuel thy mothers father: & ther take the a wyfe of the daughters of Laban thy mothers brother.
And God almyghty blesse the, encrease the, and multiply the that thou mayst be a numbre of people,
and giue the the blessing of Abraham: both to the, and to thy sede with the, that thou mayst possesse the Lande (wherein thou arte a straunger) whych God gaue vnto Abraham
Thus Isaac sent forth Iacob, to go to Messapotamia vnto Laban, sonne of Bethuell the Sirien, and brother to Rebecca Iacobs and Esaus mother.

When Esau saw that Isaac had blessed Iacob, & sent him to Mesopotamia, to fet him a wyfe thence, & that as he blessed him he gaue him a charge, saying: se thou take not a wife of the daughters of Canaan:
and that Iacob had obeyed hys father and mother, & was gone vnto Mesopotamia:
and seynge also that the daughters of Canaan pleased not Isaac hys father:
then went he vnto Ismael, and toke vnto the wyues whyche he had Mahala the daughter of Ismaell Abrahams sonne, the sister of Nabaioth to be hys wyf
Iacob departed from Berseba, and wente towarde Haran,
and came vnto a place, and taried there al nyght, bycause the sunne was downe. And toke a stone of the place, & put it vnder hys head, and layed hym downe in the same place to slepe.
And he dreamed: and behold there stode a ladder vpon the earth, & the toppe reached vp to heauen. And see, the angels of God went vp and downe vpon it,
yea, & the Lord stod vpon it, and sayed. I am the Lorde God of Abraham thy father, & the God of Isaac. The land whiche thou sleapest vpon wyl I gyue the & thy sede.
And thy sede shal be as the dust of the earth: and thou shalt spreade abrode: weste, easte, north, and south. And thorowe the and thy sede shal al the kynreds of the earth be blessed.
And se I am wyth the, and wyll be thy keper in all places whyther thou goest, and wyll brynge the agayne into thys land: neither wyll I leaue the vntyll I haue made good all that I haue promised the.
When Iacob was awaked out of his slepe he sayd: surely the Lord is in this place, & I was not aware.
And he was afrayed & said: howe fearfull is this place? it is none other: but euen the house of god, & the gate of heauen.
And Iacob stode vp early in the morning, & toke the stone that he hadde laied vnder his head, and pitched it vpon the ende, and poured oyle vpon the top of it:
And he called the name of the place Bethell, for in dede the name of the city was called Lus
before time And Iacob vowed a vowe sayinge: If God wyll be wyth me, and wyll kepe me in thys iourney whyche I goo, and wyll gyue me breade to eate, and clothes to put on,
so that I come againe vnto mi fathers house in saftye, then shall the Lorde be my God,
& thys stone whyche I haue sette vp an ende, shall be Goddes house: and of all that thou shalte gyue me, wyll I gyue the tenth vnto the.
29: Then Iacob lyfte vp hys fete, and wente towarde the east coutrye.
And as he loked aboute, beholde there was a well in the fylde, and thre flockes of shepe laye thereby (for at that well were the flockes watered) and ther lay a greate stone at the well mouth.
And the maner was to bryng the flocke thethers, and to roull the stone frome the welles mouthe, and to water the shepe, and to put the stone agayne vppon the welles mouthe vnto his place.
And Iacob sayed vnto them: brethren whence be ye? And they sayed: of Haran are we.
And he sayed vnto theym: knowe ye Laban the sonne of Nahor? And they sayed: we know hym.
And he sayed vnto theim: is he in good healthe. And they sayed he is in good healthe: and beholde hys Daughter Rachell cometh wyth the shepe.
And he sayed: lo, it is a greate whyle to nyght, neyther is it tyme that the catell shoulde be gathered togyther: water the shepe, and go & fede them.
And they sayed: we may not, vntyll all the flockes be brought togyther, and the stone be rolled from the welles mouthe, and so we water our shepe.
While he yet talked with them, Rahel came wyth hyr fathers shepe, for she kepte them.

As sone as Iacob sawe Rahell, the doughter of Laban hys mothers brother, & the shepe of Laban hys mothers brother, he went & rolled the stone from the wels mouth, & watered the shepe of Laban his mothers brother.
And Iacob kissed Rahell, & lyfte vp hys voyce & wepte:
and told hir also that he was hyr fathers brother & Rebeccas sonne. Then Rahell ranne and told hir father.
When Laban heard tell of Iacab hys sisters sonne, he ran to mete hym, & embraced him & kissed him, & brought him to his house And then Iacob tolde Laban all the matter.
And then Laban said: wel, thou art my bone & my flesh. Abide with me the space of a moneth.
And afterward Laban sayed vnto Iacob: Though thou be my brother shouldest thou therfore serue me for nought? Tell me what shal thy wages be?
And Laban had .ij. daughters, the eldest called Lea & the yongest Rahel.
Lea was tender eyed, but Rahell was beutifull & well fauoured.
And Iacob loued hyr well, and sayd: I wyl serue the seuen yere for Rahel thy yongest doughter.
And Laban answered, it is better that I gyue hyr the then to to an other manne: byde therefore wyth me.
And Iacob serued .vij. yere for Rahell, and they semed vnto hym but a fewe dayes, for the loue he had to hyr.
And Iacob sayed vnto Laban: gyue me my wyfe that I maye lye wyth hyr. For the tyme appoynted me is come.
Then Laban bade al men of that place, & made a feast.
And when euen was come, he toke Lea hys doughter & brought hir to him & he went in vnto hyr.
And Laban gaue vnto hys doughter Lea, Zilpha hys mayd, to be hyr seruaunt.
And when the morning was come, behold it was Lea. Then saied he to Laban: wherefore hast thou played thus wt me? did not I serue the for Rahell, wherfore then hast thou begyled me?
Laban answered: it is not the maner of thys place to mary the yongest before the eldest.
Passe out this weke & then shal thys also be geuen the for the seruice which thou shalt serue me yet .vij. yeres more.
And Iacob did euen so, & passed out that weke, & then he gaue him Rahel his doughter to wyfe also.
And Laban gaue to Rahell hys doughter, Bilha hys handmayd to be hir seruaunte.
So lay he by Rahell also, & loued Rahell more then Lea, and serued hym yet .vij. yere more.
When the Lord sawe that Lea was despised he made hyr fruitful: but Rahel was baren.
And Lea conceaued & bare a sonne, & called eys name Ruben, for she sayd: the Lorde hath loked vpon my tribulation. And nowe my husband wyll loue me.
And she conceaued agayne & bare a sonne, and sayd: the Lorde hath hearde that I am despysed, & hath therfore geuen me thys Sonne also, & she called hym Simeon.
And she conceaued yet, and bare a sonne and sayed: now thys once wyll my husbande kepe me companye, bycause I haue borne him thre sonnes: and therfore she called hys name Leui.
And she conceyued yet agayne, and bare a sonne sayinge: nowe wyll I prayse the Lorde: therfore she called hys name Iuda, and left bearyng.
30: When Rahel sawe that she bare Iacab no chyldren, she enuied hyr sister, and sayd vnto Iacob Geue me children, or els I am but dead.
Then was Iacob wroth wyth Rahel saying. Am I in Godds stede whyche kepeth from the, the fruite of thy wombe?
Then she said: here is my maid Bylha: go in vnto hyr, that she maye beare vpon my lappe, that I may be encreased by hyr.
And she gaue hym Bilha hyr handmaid to wyfe. And Iacob wente in vnto hyr:
and Bylha conceaued and bare Iacob a sonne.
Then said Rahel. God hath gyuen sentence on my syde, & hath also heard my voyce, and hath geuen me a sonne. Therefore called she him Dan.
And Bylha Rahels mayd conceaued agayne, and bare Iacob an other sonne.
And Rahel sayd: God is turned, and I haue made a chaunge wyth my syster, and haue gotten the vpper hande. And she called hys name: Nepthaly.
When Lea sawe that she had left bearing she toke Silpha hyr mayd, and gaue hyr Iacob to wyfe.
And Silpha Leas mayed bare Iacob a sonne.
Then sayed Lea: Good luck: & called his name Gad.
And Silpha Leas mayd bare Iacob an other sonne.
Then sayd Lea: happy am I, for the doughters wil call me blessed. And called his name Asser.
And Ruben wente out in the wheate haruest, and founde mandragoras in the fyldes, and brought them vnto his mother Lea Then sayd Rahel to Lea giue me of thy sonnes mandragoras.

And Lea answered. Is it not inoughe that thou haste taken away my husband, but wouldest take away my sons mandragoras also. Then sayed Rahel: wel, let hym slepe wyth the thys nyghte, for thy sonnes mandragoras.
And when Iacob came from the fyeldes at euen, Lea wente oute to mete hym, and sayed: come in to me, for I haue bought the wyth my sonnes mandragoras. And he slept wyth hyr that nyght.
And God hearde Lea, that shee conceaued and bare vnto Iacob the fyft sonne.
Then sayed Lea. God hath geuen me my rewarde, bycause I gaue my mayden to my husbande, and she called hym Isachar.
And Lea conceaued yet agayne, and bare Iacob the syxt sonne.
Then sayed she. God hath endewed me wyth a good dowrye. Nowe wyll my husbande dwell wyth me, bycause I haue borne him syxe sonnes: and called hys name Zabulon.
After that she bare a daughter, & called hyr Dina.
And God remembred Rahel, heard hir, & made hyr fruitefull:
so that she conceaued & bare a sonne & said: God hath taken away my rebuke.
And she called hys name Ioseph, saying. The Lord giue me yet an other sonne.
As sone as Rahel had borne Ioseph, Iacob said to Laban. Send me awaye that I may go vnto myne own place & contrey,
gyue me my wiues & my children for whom I haue serued the, and let me goo: for thou knowest what seruice I haue done the.
Then sayd Laban vnto hym: If I haue founde fauoure in thy syght (for I suppose that the Lorde hath blessed me for thy sake)
apoint what thy rewarde shall be, and I will geue it the.
But he sayde vnto hym: thou knoweste what seruyce I haue done the, and in what takyng the catell haue bene vnder me:
For it was but lytle that thou haddest before I came, & now it is increased into a multytude, & the Lord hath blessed the for my sake. But now when shal I make prouision for myne owne house also.
And he sayd: what shall I then geue the? And Iacob answered: thou shalt geue me nothyng at al, if thou wylt do thys one thynge for me: and then wyll I turne agayne, and fede thy shepe and kepe them.

I will go aboute all thy shepe thys day, & seperate from them all the shepe that are spotted & of diuers colours, & all blacke sheepe among the lambes, & the party, and the spotted among the kyddes: & the same shall be my reward.

So shall my ryghtuousnes answere for me: when the tyme cometh that I shal receiue mi reward of the: so that whatsoeuer is not speckled & party amonge the gotes & blacke among the lambes, let that be theft with me.
Then sayd Laban: Loo, I am content, that it be accordyng as thou hast sayed.

And he toke out that same daye the he gootes that were party & of diuers colours, and all the she gootes that were spotted, & party coloured, & all that had whyte in them, & all the blacke amonge the Lambes: & put theim in the kepynge of hys Sonnes,
and sette three dayes iourney betwyxte hym selfe and Iacob. Ind so Iacob kepte the reste of Labans shepe.
Iacob toke roddes of grene popular, hasel & of chestnottrees, & pylled white strakes in them, & made the white apeare in the staues:
And he put the staues whiche he had pilled, euen before the shepe in the gutters & watring troughes, when the shepe came to dryncke: that they shold conceyue when they came to drynke.
And the shepe conceyued before the staues, & brought forth straked, spotted, and party.

Then Iacob parted the lambes and turned the faces of the shepe toward the spotted things, & toward al maner of blake thinges thorow out the flockes of Laban. And he made him flockes of his own by them selfe, whiche he put not vnto the flockes of Laban.
And alwaye in firste buckinge tyme of the shepe, Iacob put the staues before the shepe in the gutters, that they might conceyue before the staues:
but in the later bucking time he put them not ther: so the laste brode was Labans, & the fyrst Iacobs.
And the manne became exceading rich and had many shepe, mayedseruauntes, menseruauntes, camels and asses.
31: And Iacob hearde the wordes of Labans sonnes howe they sayed: Iacob hathe taken awaye all that was our fathers & of our fathers goods hath he gotten all hys honour.
And Iacob beheld the countenaunce of Laban, that it was not toward hym as it was in tymes paste.
And the Lorde sayed vnto Iacob: turne agayne into the Land of thy fathers & to thy kynred, & I wyll be wyth the.
Then Iacob sent & called Rahell & Lea to the fyelde vnto hys shepe,
& sayd vnto them: I se your fathers countenaunce, that it is not towarde me as in tymes past. Moreouer the god of my father hath bene wyth me.
And ye know how that I haue serued your father with al mi might.
And your father hath deceyued me, & chaunged mi wages .x. times: but God suffred him not to hurt me.
When he sayed the spotted shall be thy wages, then all the sheepe were spotted. If he sayd the straked shall be thy reward, then were all the shepe straked:
thus hath God taken away your fathers cattel & geuen them me.
For in bucking tyme I lifted vp myne eyes, & sawe in a dreame, & beholde the rammes that bucked the shepe were straked spotted, & party.
And the angel of god spake vnto me in a dreame, saiyng: Iacob? And I answered: here am I.
And he sayed lyft vp thine eyes & se, howe al the rammes that leape vpon the shepe are straked, spotted & party: for I haue sene al that Laban doth vnto th
I am the god of Bethel wher thou anointedst the stone, & wher thou vowedst a vow vnto me. Now arise & get the out of this country, & return vnto the land wher thou was borne.
Then answered Rahell & Lea, & sayed vnto him: we haue no parte nor enheritaunce in oure fathers house,
he counteth vs euen vs straungers, for he hath solde vs, & hath euen eaten vp the price of vs.
Moreouer al the riches which God hath taken from our father, that is ours & our children. Nowe therfore whatsoeuer God hath sayd vnto the that do.
Then Iacob rose vp, & sett his sonnes & wyues vp vpon camels,
& caried away al his cattel & al his substaunce which he had gotten in Mesopotamia, for to go to Isaac his father vnto the land of Canaan.
Laban was gone to shere his shepe, & Rahel had stolen hir fathers images.
And Iacob stale away the herte of Laban the Syrien, in that he tolde hym not that he fledde.
So fled he and all that he had, and made hym selfe readye, and passed ouer the ryuers, and sette hys face strayght ouer the mounte Gilead.
Vpon the third day after, was it told Laban that Iacob fled.
Then he toke his brethren wt him & folowed after hym .vij. dayes iourney, & ouertoke him at the mount Gilead.
And God came to Laban the Syrian in a dreame by nyght, & sayd vnto him: take hede to thy selfe, that thou speake not to Iacob ought saue good.
And Laban ouertoke Iacob: & Iacob had pitched his tent in the mount. And Laban wt hys brethren pytched their tent also vpon the mounte Giliad.
Then sayd Laban to Iacob: Why hast thou thys done to steale awaye my herte, and carye awaye my daughters as though thei had bene take captyue wt the swerde?
Wherfore wentest thou away secreatly vnknowne to me, and didest not tel me, that I might haue brought the on the way wt myrth, singyng, timrels and harpes,
& haste not suffered me to kisse my chyldren & my daughters? Thou wast a fole to do it,
for I am able to do you euyl. But the God of youre father spake vnto me yesterday saying: take hede that thou speake not to Iacob ought saue good.
And now thoughe thou wentest away, bicause thou longest after thi fathers house, yet wherfore hast thou stolen my Goddes.
Iacob answered & sayed to Laban: bicause I was afraied, & thought that thou woldest haue taken away thy daughters fro me.
But with whomesoeuer thou findest thy Gods, let hym dye here before our brethren. Seke that thyne is by me, & take it to the: for Iacob wist not that Rahel had stolen them.
Then went Laban into Iacobs tente, & into Leas tente, & into .ii. maddens tentes: but founde them not. Then went he out of Leas tent, & entred into Rahels tente.
And Rahel toke the Images & put them in the camels strawe & sate downe vpon them. And Laban searched all the tente but found them not.
Then sayd she to hir father, my Lorde, be not angrye that I can not ryse vp before the, for the disease of women is come vpon me. So searched he but found them not.
Iacob was wrooth & chode with Laban. Iacob also answered and sayd to him: what haue I trespaced or what haue I offended, that thou folowest after me?
Thou hast searched all my stuffe, and what hast thou founde of al thy houshold stuffe? put it here before thy brethren & myne, & let them Iudge betwexte vs both.
Thys .xx. yere that I haue bene wt the thy shepe, & thy gotes haue not bene barren, & the rammes of thy flocke haue I not eaten.
Whatsoeuer was torne of beastes I brought it not vnto the, but made it good mi selfe of my hande dyddest thou requyre it, whether it was stollen by day or nyght.
Moreouer by daye the heate consumed me, and the colde by nyghte, and my slepe departed fro myne eyes.
Thus haue I bene .xx. yere in thy house, & serued the .xiiij. yeres for thy .ij. daughters and .vi. yere for thy shepe, & thou hast chaunged my rewarde .x. tymes.

And excepte the God of my father, the God of Abraham, & the God whome Isaac feareth, had bene wyth me: surely thou haddest sent me away now al empty. But God beheld my tribulation, and the labour of my handes: and rebuked the yesterdaye.

Laban answered & sayed vnto Iacob: the daughters are my daughters, & the children are my chyldren, & the shepe are my shepe, & al that thou seest is myne. And what can I do thys day vnto these my doughters, or vnto their children which thei haue borne?
Now therfore come on: let vs make a bond, I and thou togyther, & let it be a wytnes betwene the & me.
Then toke Iacob a stone and set it vp an ende,
and sayed vnto his brethren, gather stones. And they toke stones, & made an heape, and they ate ther vpon the heape.
And Laban called it Iegar Sahadutha, but Iacob called it Gilead.
Then sayed Laban: thys heape be wytnes betwene the & me this day (therfore is it called Gilead)
& this totehil which the Lord seeth (sayd he) be wytnesse betwene me and the when we are departed one from another
that thou shalt not vexe my daughters neyther shalt take other wyues vnto them. Here is no man wyth vs: behold God is wytnes betwyxt the and me.
And Laban sayd more ouer to Iacob: beholde, this heape and thys marke whych I had set here, betwyxte me, & the:
this heape be wytnesse & also this marke that I wyll not come ouer this heape to the, & thou shalte not come ouer thys heape and marke to do any harme.
The God of Abraham, the God of Nahor, & the God of their fathers be Iudge betwyxt vs. And Iacob sware by him that his father Isaac feared.
Then Iacob did sacrifice vpon the mounte, and called hys brethren to eate bread. And they ate breade & taried al nyght in the hyll.
And early in the morning Laban rose vp & kyssed hys chyldren and his daughters, & blessed them & departed and went vnto hys place agayne.
32: But Iacob went forth on his iourney. And the angels of God came & met hym.
And when Iacob sawe them, he said, thys is Gods hoost: & called the name of that same place, Mahanaim.
Iacob sent messengers before him to Esau hys brother, vnto the land of Seir, and the fyeld of Edom
And he commaunded theym sayinge: see that ye speake after thys maner to my Lord Esau: thy seruaunte Iacob sayeth thus. I haue soiourned and bene a straunger wyth Laban vnto thys time,
and haue gotten oxen, asses, and shepe, menseruauntes & womenseruauntes, & haue sent to shew it my Lord, that I may finde grace in thy sight.
And the messengers came againe to Iacob sayinge: we came vnto thi brother Esau, & he commeth agaynst the & .iiij. hundred men wyth him.
Then was Iacob greatly afrayed, & wyste not whych way to turne him selfe, and deuided the people that was wyth hym, and the shepe, oxen, & camels, into .ij. companyes,
& sayd: If Esau come to the one part & smite it the other maye saue it selfe.
And Iacob said: O god of mi father Abraham, & God of my father Isaac: Lord whiche saydest vnto me, returne vnto thy countrye & to thy kynred, & I wyll do all well with the.
I am not worthy of the leaste of all the mercies & trueth whyche thou hast shewed vnto thy seruaunt. For wyth my stafe came I ouer thys Iordane, & now haue I goten two droues.
Deliuer me from the handes of my brother Esau: for I feare hym: least he wyll come and smyte the mother wyth the chyldren.
Thou saydest that thou wouldest surely do me good, and wouldest make my sede as the sande of the sea, whyche canne not be numbred for multitude.
And he taried ther that same nyghte, and toke of that which came to hand a present, vnto Esau hys brother
.ij. hundred she gootes, and .xx. he gootes: .ij. hundred shepe, and .xx. rammes:
thyrtye mylch camels wyth their coltes .xl. kyne, and .x. bulles .xx. she asses, & .x. foles,
and deliuered theym vnto hys seruauntes, euery droue by them selues, & said vnto theim, go forth before me & put a space betwyxte euerye droue.
And he commaunded the formest sayinge. When Esau mi brother meteth the & axeth the sayinge: whose seruaunte arte thou and whither goest thou, and whose are these that go before the:
thou shalte say they be thy seruaunt Iacobs, and are a present sent vnto my Lorde Esau, and beholde he him selfe commeth after vs.
And so commaunded he the second, & euen so the thyrd, & likewise al that folowed the droues sayinge, of this maner se that ye speake vnto Esau saying when ye mete hym,

& said moreouer. Behold thy seruaunt Iacob cometh after vs, for he said. I wyl pease his wrath wt the present that goth before me, and afterward I wil se hym my selfe, so peraduenture he wil receiue me to grace.
So wente the present before hym and he taried all that nyght in the tent,
and rose vp the same night and toke hys two wyues, and his two maydens and hys .xi. sonnes, and went ouer the fourd Iabok.
And he toke them and sent them ouer the ryuer, and sente ouer that he had,
& taried behind hym selfe alone. And ther wresteled a man wyth him vnto the breaking of the day.
And when he sawe that he could not preuayle agaynste hym, he smote hym vnder the thye, & the senowe of Iacobs thye shranke as he wrestled with him
And he said: let me goo, for the day breaketh. And he said: I wyll not lette the go, excepte thou blesse me.
And he sayd vnto hym: what is thy name? He answered: Iacob.
And he said: thou shalt be called Iacob no more, but Israel. For thou hast wresteled with God and hast preuayled.
And Iacob asked hym sayinge, tell me thy name. And he said, wherfore doest thou aske after my name? & he blessed hym there.
And Iacob called the name of that place Pheniel for I haue sene God face to face, & yet is my life reserued.
And as he went ouer Pheniel the sonne rose vpon him, & he halted vpon his thye:
wherfore the children of Israell eate not of the senow that shranke vnder the thye, vnto thys daye: bicause that he smote Iacob vnder the thye in the senowe that shroncke.
33: Iacob lift vp hys eyes & sawe hys brother Esau come, & wyth hym .iiij. hundred men. And he deuided the chyldren vnto Lea and vnto Rahell, and vnto the two maydens.
And he put the maydens and theyr chyldren formost, & Lea & hir children after, & Rahell & Iosephe hindermost.
And he went before them & fell on the ground .vij. times, vntyll he came vnto hys brother.
Esau ranne to mete hym & enbraced hym and fell on his necke & kissed hym, and they wepte.
And he lyfte vp hys eyes & sawe the wyues & theyr chyldren, & said: what are these which thou there hast? And he sayd they are the children which god hath geuen thy seruaunt
Then came the maydens forthe, & dyd theyr obeysaunce.
Lea also & hir chyldren came and dyd theyr obeysaunce. And laste of all came Ioseph & Rahel and dyd theyr obeysaunce.
And he sayed: what meanest thou wt all the drooues which I mette. And he answered: to fynd grace in the syghte of my Lorde.
And Esau saied: I haue inough my brother, kepe that thou hast vnto thy selfe.
Iacob answered: Oh naye, but if I haue founde grace in thy syght, receyue my presente of my hande: for I haue sene thy face as though I had sene the face of god:
wherfore receiue me to grace & take my blessinge that I haue brought the, for god hath geuen it me. And I haue inough of al thinges. And so he compelled him to take it.
And he sayd: let vs take our iourney, and goo, and I wyll go in thy company.
And he said vnto him: my lord knoweth that I haue tender children, ewes, & kine with yong, vnder myne hand, whych if men shoulde ouerdriue but euen one day, the whole flocke wold dye.
Let my Lord therfore go before his seruaunte, and I wyl dryue fayre and softly, accordyng as the cattell that goth before me, & the chyldren, be able to endure: vntyll I come to my Lord vnto Seir.
And Esau said: let me yet leaue some of my folke with the. And he sayed: what neadeth it? let me find grace in the syght of my Lord.
So Esau wente his waye agayne that same daye vnto Seyr.
And Iacob toke hys iourney toward Sucoth, and built him a house, and made boothes for hys catell: wherof the name of the place is called Sucoth.
And Iacob came peasably into the cytye of Sichem in the Lande of Canaan, after that he was come from Messopotamia, & pytched before the citye,
& bought a percel of ground wher he pytched hys tent, of the chyldren of Hemor Sichems father, for an hundred lambes.
And he made ther an aulter, & there called vpon the myghty God of Israel.
34: Dina the doughter of Lea whiche she bare to Iacob, went out to se the doughters of the land.
And Sichem the sonne of Hemor the Heuite Lorde of the countrey, saw hyr, and toke hyr, and lay with hyr, and forced hir:
and his herte lay vnto Dina the daughter of Iacob. And he loued that damsell, & spake kyndly vnto hyr,
and spake vnto hys father Hemor saying, get me thys mayden vnto my wyfe.
And Iacob hearde that he had defiled Dina hys daughter, but hys sonnes were wyth the cattel in the felde, and therfore he helde hys peace, vntyl they were come.
Then Hemor the father of Sichem went out vnto Iacob, to comen with hym.

And the sonnes of Iacob came out of the field as sone as they heard it, for it greued them, & thei were not a little wroth bycause he had wroughte folly in Israel, in that he had lyed wt Iacobs doughter, whyche thynge oughte not to be done.
And Hemor comened with them saying? The soule of my sonne Sichem longeth for your doughter: giue hyr hym to wife,
& make mariages wt vs: giue your doughters vnto vs, & take our doughters vnto you,
& dwel with vs & the land shal be at your pleasure, dwel & do your busines, & haue your possessions therein.
And Sichem sayed vnto hyr father & hyr brethren: lette me fynde grace in your eyes, & whatsoeuer ye appoint me, that wyl I gyue.
Axe frely of me both the dowry and gyftes, & I wyll giue accordynge as ye saye vnto me, & gyue me the damsel to wyfe.
Then the sonnes of Iacob answered to Sichem & Hemor hys father deceytfullye, because he had defiled Dina theyr sister.
And they sayd vnto them, we can not do thys thing that we shoulde gyue our syster to one that is vncircumcised, for that were a shame vnto vs.
Only in thys wyl we consent vnto you? If ye wyl be as we be, that all the men children amonge you be circumcised,
then wyll we gyue our doughter to you & take youres to vs, & wil dwell with you & be one people.
But & if ye wyll not herken vnto vs to be circumcised, then wyll we take oure doughter and go our waies.
And their words pleased Hemor: & Sichem his sonne.
And the yonge man deferred not but to do the thyng, bicause he had a lust to Iacobs doughter: he was also most set by of all that were in hys fathers house.
Then Hemor & Sichem wente vnto the gate of theyr citye, & comuned with the men of theyr city saying:
these men are peaceable with vs, & wyl dwel in the land and do their occupation therin. And in the lande is rowme inoughe for them, let vs take theyr doughters to wyues & gyue them ours:
only herein wyll they consent vnto vs for to dwel with vs & to be one people: if all the men children that are among vs be circumcised as they are.
Their goodes and their substaunce, & all theyr cattel are ours, only let vs consent vnto them, that they may dwell with vs.
And vnto Hemor and Sichem hys sonne harkened al that went out at the gate of hys city. And al the men children were circumcised whatsoeuer went out at the gates of his city.
And the thyrd day when it was paynfull to them .ij. two of the sons of Iacob Simeon, & Leuy Dinas brethren, toke either of them his swerd & went into the citye boldly, & slewe al that was male,
and slewe also Hemor and Sichem his sonne wt the edge of the swerde, and toke Dina their syster oute of Sichems house, and went theyr way.
Then came the sonnes of Iacob vpon the dead, & spoyled the city, bicause they had defyled theyr syster:
and toke theyr shepe, oxen asses and what so euer was in the citye, and also in the fyeldes.
And all theyr goodes, all theyr chyldren, and theyr wyues toke they captiue and made hauocke of al that was in the houses.

And Iacob sayd to Simeon and Leui: ye haue troubled me and made me stincke vnto the inhabitours of the Lande, boeth to the Canaanites and also vnto the Pherezites. And I am a fewe in numbre. Wherefore they shal gather them selues togyther against me & slee me, & so shal I and my house be destroied.
And they answered: shold they deale with our sister as wyth an whore.
35: And God sayd vnto Iacob, aryse & get the vp to Bethel, and dwell there. And make ther an aultare vnto God that appered vnto the when thou fleddest from Esau thy brother.
Then sayd Iacob vnto hys houshold & to all that were with him, put away the straunge Goddes that are amonge you, and make your selues cleane, and chaunge your garmentes,
and let vs arise and go vp to Bethel, that I may make an aulter there vnto God, whyche hearde me in the day of my tribulation and was wyth me in the waye whyche I wente.
And they gaue vnto Iacob all the straunge Gods whych were vnder theyr handes, & al theyr earynges which were in theyr eares, & Iacob hid them vnder an oke at Sichem.
And they departed. And the feare of God fel vpon the cities that were rounde aboute them, that they durste not folowe after the sonnes of Iacob.
So came Iacob to Lus in the land of Canaan, otherwise called Bethell, wyth all the people that was wyth hym.
And he builded there an aulter, and called the place Bethel: bicause that god appeared vnto him there, when he fled from hys brother.
Then dyed Debora Rebeccas norsse, & was buryed beneth Bethell vnder an ooke. And the name of it was called the oke of lamentation.
And God appeared vnto Iacob againe after he came oute of Messopotamia & blessed him,
& saied vnto him: thy name is Iacob. Notwithstandinge thou shalt be no more called Iacob, but Israell shall be thy name. And so was hys name called Israell.
And God sayd vnto hym: I am God almighty, growe & multiplye: for people and a multitude of people shall sprynge of the, yea & kinges shal come out of thy loynes.
And the Land whych I gaue Abraham & Isaac wyl I giue vnto the, & vnto thy sede after the wyl I gyue it also.
And God departed from him in the place where he talked wyth hym.
And Iacob set vp a marke in the place where he talked with hym: euen a pilloue of stone, & poured drynke offeryng thereon, & poured also oyle thereon,
& called the name of the place wher God spake with him, Bethel.
And they departed from Bethell, & when he was but a feld breath from Ephrath, Rahel began to trauel. And in trauelynge she was in perell.
And as she was in paynes of hyr laboure the mydwyfe sayed vnto hir: feare not, for thou shalt haue thys sonne also.
Then as hyr soule was a departynge, that she must die, she called his name BenOni. But his father called him BenIamyn.
And thus died Rahel & was buried in the way to Ephrath which nowe is called Bethlehem.
And Iacob sette vp a piller vpon hir graue, whych is called Rahelles graue piller vnto thys daye.
And Israel went thence & pytched vp his tent beyond the tower of Eder.
And it chaunced as Israel dwelt in that lande, that Ruben went & laye wyth Bilha hys fathers concubyne, and it came to Israels eare. The sonnes of Iacob were .xij. in numbre.
The sonnes of Lea. Ruben Iacobs eldest sonne, and Simeon, Leui, Iuda, Isachar, & Zabulon.
The sonnes of Rahell: Ioseph & BenIamin.
The sonnes of Bilha Rahels mayde: Dan and Nepthali.
The sonnes of Zilpha Leas mayde, Gad and Aser. These are the sonnes of Iacob whyche were borne hym in Messopotamia.
Then Iacob went vnto Isaac his father to Mamre a principal city, otherwise called Hebron: where Abraham & Isaac soieourned as straungers.
And the dayes of Isaac were an hundred & .lxxx. yeres:
& then fell he sycke & dyed, & was put vnto his people beyng olde and full of dayes. And his sonnes Esau and Iacob buried him.
36: These are the generations of Esau which is called Edom.
Esau toke hys wyues of the doughters of Canaan, Ada the doughter of Elon an Hethite, & Ahalibama the daughter of Ana, which Ana was the sone of Zibeon an Heuite.
And Basmath Ismaels daughter & sister of Nebaioth.
And Ada bare vnto Esau Eliphas: & Basmath bare Regue.
And Ahalibama bare Ieus, Iaelam, & Korah. These ar the sons of Esau which were borne him in the land of Canaan.

And Esau toke hys wyues, hys sonnes & daughteres & all the soules of hys house: his goodes and al hys cattel & al hys substaunce whych he had gott in the lande of Canaan, and wente into a contrey awaye frome hys brother Iacob:
for theyr rychesse was so much, that they could not dwel togyther, & that the lande wherin they were straungers, could not receiue them: bicause of theyr cattell.
Thus dwelte Esau in the mounte Seir, which Esau is called Edom.
These are the generations of Esau father of the Edomites in mounte Seir,
& these are the names of Esaus sonnes: Eliphas the sonne of Ada, the wife of Esau, & Reguell the sonne of Basmath the wife of Esau also.
And the sonnes of Eliphas were. Theman, Omar, Zepho, Gaetham and Kenas.
And Thimna was concubine to Eliphas Esaus son, & bare vnto Eliphas Amalech. And these be the sonnes of Ada Esaus wyfe.
And these are the sons of Reguel: Nahath, Serah, Samma, and Misa: these were the sonnes of Basmath Esaus wyfe.
And these were the sonnes of Ahalibama Esaus wyfe the daughter of Ana, sonne of Zebeon whyche she bare vnto Esau: Ieus, Iealam, and Roah.
These were dukes of the sonnes of Esau. The chyldren of Eliphas the fyrst sonne of Esau were these: duke Theman, duke Omar, duke Zepho, duke Kenas,
duke Korah, duke Gaetham, & duke Amalech: these are the dukes that came of Eliphas in the lande of Edom, & these were the sonnes of Ada.

These were the children of Reguel Esaus sone: duke Nahath, duke Serah, duke Samma, duke Missa. These are the dukes that came of Reguel in the Land of Edom, and these were the sonnes of Basmath Esaus wife.
These were the children of Ahalibama Esaus wyfe: duke Ieus duke Gaelan, duke Korah, these dukes came of Ahalibama the doughter of Ana Esaus wyfe.
These are the children of Esau, & these are the dukes of them: which Esau is called Edom.
These are the children if Seir the Horite the inhabitoure of the Lande: Lothan, Soball, Zibeon, Ana,
Dison, Eser, & Disan. These are the Dukes of the Horites the chyldren of Seir, in the Lande of Edomme.
And the chyldren of Lothan were: Hori and Heman. And Lothans syster was called Thimna.
The chyldren of Sobal were these: Aluan, Manahath, Ebal, Sepho, & Onam.
These were the children of Zibeon, Aia & Ana, thys was that Ana that found the mules in the wildernes, as he fed hys father Zibeons asses.
The children of Ana were these. Dison, & Ahalibama the doughter of Ana.
These ar the children of Dison, Hemdan, Esban, Iethran, & Cheran.
The children of Ezer were these, Bilhan, Seauan, & Akan.
The children of Disan were: vz & Aran.
These are the dukes that came of Hori: duke Lothan, duke Saball, duke Zibeon, duke Ana,
duke Dison, duke Ezet, duke Disan. These be the dukes that came of Hory in theyr dukedoms in the land of Seir.
These are the kynges that reigned in the land of Edom before there raygned any kynge amonge the chyldren of Israel,
Bela the sonne of Beor raygned in Edomea, & the name of hys city was Dinhaba.
And when Bela dyed, Iobab the sonne of Serah oute of Bezara, reigned in his steade.
When Iobab was dead, Husam of the land of Themany reygned in hys stede,
And after the death of Husem, Hadad the sonne of Bedad which slew the Madianites in the feyld of the Moabites, reigned in his stead, & the name of hys city was Auith.
When Hadad was deade, Samla of Masteka reigned in hys stead.
When Samla was deade, Saule of the ryuer Rehoboth reygned in hys steade.
When Saul was deade, Baal Hanam the sonne of Achbor reygned in hys steade.
And after the deathe of Baal Hanan the sonne of Achbor, Hadad reygned in hys steade, & the name of the city was Pagu. And hys wyues name Mehetabeell the doughter of Matred the daughter of Mesaab.
These are the names of the dukes that came of Esau, in the .xij. kynredes, places & names: Duke Thimma, duke Alua, duke Ietheth,
Duke Ahalibana, Duke Ela, duke Pinon,
duke Kenas, duke Theman, duke Mibzar,
duke Magdiel, duke Iram. These be the dukes of Edomea in theyr habitations, in the Lande of theyr possessions. Thys Esau is the father of the Edomites.
37: And Iacob dwelt in the Lande wherin his father was a straunger, that is to saye in the Land of Canaan.

And these are the generations of Iacob, when Iosephe was .xvij. yere olde, he kepte shepe wyth hys brethren, and the ladde was wyth the sonnes of Bilha and of Zilpha hys fathers wyues. And he brought vnto theyr father an euil sayinge that was of them.
And Israel loued Ioseph more then al his chyldren bicause he begate hym in hys olde age, and he made him a cote of many colours.
When hys brethren sawe that theyr father loued hym more then all his brethren, they hated him, & could not speake one kinde worde vnto hym.
Moreouer Iosephe dreamed a dreame & told it his brethren: wherfore they hated him yet the more.
And he sayed vnto them heare I praye you thys dreame whyche I haue dreamed:
Beholde we were makynge sheues in the field: & lo, my sheffe arose and stode vpryght, & youres stode round aboute and made obeysaunce to my shefe.
Than sayd hys brethren vnto hym: what, shalt thou be our kyng or shalt thou reygne ouer vs? And they hated him yet the more, because of hys dreame and of hys wordes.
And he dreamed yet another dreame & told it his brethren sayinge: beholde, I haue had one dreame more: me thought the sonne and the moone and .xi. starres made obeysaunce to me.

And when he had told it vnto his father and his brethren, hys father rebuked hym & sayde vnto him: what meaneth this dreame which thou hast dreamed: shal I and thy mother and thy brethren come and fall on the grounde before the?
And his brethren hated him, but his father noted the saying.
His brethren went to kepe their fathers shepe in Sichem,
and Israel sayde vnto Ioseph: do not thy brethren kepe in Sichem? come that I may sende the to them. And he answered here am I.
And he sayde vnto hym: go & see whether it be well wyth thy brethren and the shepe, and brynge me worde agayne. And sent hym out of the vale of Hebron, for to go to Sichem.
And a certayne man founde hym wandrynge out of his way in the felde, and axed hym what he soughte.
And he answered: I seke my brethren, tell me I praye the where they kepe shepe.
And the man said: they are departed hence, for I herde them say let vs goo vnto Dothan. Thus went Ioseph after hys brethren, and founde them in Dothan.
And when they sawe him a farre of before he came at them, they toke councell agaynst him, for to sley him,
and sayd one to another, Beholde thys dreamer cometh,
come nowe and let vs sley hym and caste hym in to some pytt, and let vs saye that some wycked beast hath deuoured him, and let vs see what hys dreames wyl come to.
When Ruben herde that, he went aboute to ryd hym out of their handes and sayd, let vs not kyl hym.

And Ruben sayde moreouer vnto them, shede not his bloud, but cast him in to this pytt that is in the wyldernes, and laye no handes vpon him: for he wolde haue rydd hym out of their handes and delyuered him to his father agayn.
And as soone as Ioseph was come vnto hys brethren, they strypte hym oute of hys gay coote that was vpon hym,
and they toke hym and caste hym in to a pyt: But the pyt was emptie and had no water therein.

And they satt them doune to eate breade. And as they lyft vp their eyes and loked aboute, there came a companye of Ismaelites from Gilead, and their camels laden wyth spicery baulme, and myrre, and were goynge doune into Egypte.
Than sayde Iuda to hys brethren, what auayleth it that we sley oure brother, & kepe hys bloude secret?
come on, let vs sell hym to the Ismaelites, & let not our handes be defyled vpon him: for he is our brother and our flesh. And his brethren were content.
Than as the Madianites marchaunt men passed by, they drewe Ioseph out of the pyt & solde hym vnto the Ismaelites for .xx. peces of syluer. And they brought him into Egypte.
And when Ruben came agayne vnto the pyt and found not Ioseph there, he rent hys cloothes
and went agayne vnto his brethren saying: the lad is not yonder, & whether shall I go?
And they toke Ioseps coote and kylled a goote, & dypped the coote in the bloud.
And they sent that gay coote and caused it to be brought vnto their father and sayde: Thys haue we founde: se, whether it be thy sonnes coote or no.
And he knewe it sayinge: it is my sonnes coote, a wicked beast hath deuoured hym, and Ioseph is rent in peces.
And Iacob rent hys cloothes, and put sacke cloth about hys loynes, and sorowed for hys sonne a longe season.
Than came all hys sonnes and all hys doughters to comforte him. And he wold not be comforted, but sayde: I wyll go doune in to the graue vnto my sonne, mournynge. And thus his father wepte for hym.
And the Madianytes solde hym in Egypte vnto Putiphar a Lorde of Phoraos: & hys chefe marshall.
38: And it fortuned at that tyme that Iudas went from his brethren & gat him to a man called Hira of Odollam,
& there he sawe the daughter of a man called Sua & Canaanyte: And he toke her and went in vnto her.
And she conceyued & bare a sonne and called hys name Er.
And she conceyued agayne and bare a sonne & called him Onan.
And she conceyued the thyrde tyme & bare a sonne, whom she called Sela: and he was at Chesyb when she bare him.
And Iudas gaue Er hys Eldest sonne a wyfe whose name was Thamar.
But thys Er Iudas eldest sonne was wicked in the syght of the Lord, wherfore the Lorde slewe him.
Than sayde Iudas vnto Onan: goo into thy brothers wyfe & marye her, and styrre vp seed vnto thy brother.
And when Onan perceyued that the seed should not be hys: therfore when he went in to hys brothers wyfe, he spylled it on the ground, because he wolde not geue seed vnto his brother.
And the thyng whych he dyd, dyspleased the Lorde, wherfore he slewe hym also.

Than sayde Iudas to Thamar hys daughter in lawe: remayne a wydow at thy fathers house, tyll Sela my sonne be growne: for he feared lest he should haue dyed also, as hys brethren dyd. Thus went Thamar & dwelt in hyr fathers house.
And in processe of tyme, the daughter of Sua Iudas wyfe dyed. Than Iudas when he had left mornynge, went vnto hys shepe sherers to Thymnath with his frende Hira of Odollam.
And one told Thamar sayinge: beholde, thy father in lawe goth vp to Thymnathe, to shere hys shepe.

And she pute hyr wyddows garments of from her & couered her wyth a clooke, & dysguysed her self: And sat her downe at the enterynge of Enaim which is by the heye waye syde to Thymnath, for because she sawe that Sela was growne, and she was not geuen vnto hym to wyfe.
When Iuda sawe her, he thought it had bene an whoore, because she had couered her face.
And turned to her vnto the waye and sayde, come I praye the, let me lye wyth the, for he knewe not that it was his daughter in lawe. And she sayd what wylt thou geue me for to lye wt me?
Than sayde he, I wyl sende the a kydd from the flocke. She answered, Than geue me a pledge tyl thou send it.
Than sayde he, what pledge shall I geue the? And she sayde: thy sygnet, thy bracelet, and thy staffe that is in thy hande. And he gaue it her & lay by her, & she was whith childe by him.
And she gather vp & went & put her mantell from her, and put on her wydowes rayment agayn.
And Iudas sent the kydd by his neybure of Odollam, for to fetch out his pledge agayn from the wyfes hande. But he found her not.
Than asked he the men of the same place sayinge: where is the whoore that sat at Enaim in the waye? And they sayde: there was no whoore here.
And he came to Iuda agayne sayinge: I can not fynde her, & also the men of the place sayd: that there was no whoore there.
And Iuda sayde: let her take it to her, lest we be shamed: for I sent the kydd and thou couldest not fynde her.
And it came to passe that after .iij. monethes, one tolde Iuda sayinge: Thamar thy daughter in lawe hath played the whoore, & wyth playinge the whoore is become greate wt chylde.

And Iuda sayde: brynge her forth & let her be brente. And when they brought her forth, she sent to her father in law saying: by the man vnto whome these thynges pertayne, am I wyth chylde. And sayd also: loke whose are thys seall, bracelet, and staffe.
And Iuda knewe them saying: she is more ryghtwes than I, because I gaue her not to Sela my sonne. But he lay with her nomore.
When tyme was come that she shulde be delyuered, beholde there was two twynnes in her wombe.
And as she traueled, the one put out hys hande and the mydwyfe toke & bound a redde threde aboute it sayinge: thys wyll come oute fyrste.
But he plucked hys hande backe agayne, and hys brother came out. And she sayd: wherfore hast thou rent a rent vpon the? and called hym Pharez.
And afterwarde came oute his brother that had the rede threde about his hande, whyche was, called Zarah.
39: Ioseph was brought vnto Egypte, and Putiphar a Lorde of Pharaos: & his chefe marshal an Egyptian, bought him of the Ismaelites which brought him thyther.
And the Lorde was wyth Ioseph, & he was a luckie felowe and continued in the house of his master the Egyptian.
And hys mayster sawe that the Lorde was wyth hym, and that the Lorde made all that he dyd prosper in hys hande:
Wherfore he founde grace in his masters syghte, and serued him. And hys mayster made hym ruelar of hys house, and put al that he had in hys hand.

And as soone as he had made him ruelar ouer his house & ouer al that he had, the Lorde blessed this Egyptians house for Ioseps sake, and the blessynge of the Lorde was vpon all that he had: both in the house & also in the feldes.
And therfore he left all that he had in Iosephs hande, & loked vpon nothing that was with him, saue only on the bread which he ate. And Ioseph was a goodly persone and a wel fauored.
And it fortuned after thys, that hys masters wyfe cast her eyes vpon Ioseph & sayd: come lye with me.
But he denyed & sayde to her: Beholde, my master woteth not what he hath in the house wt me, but hath commytted all that he hath to my hande.
He him selfe is not greater in the house than I, and hath kepte nothyng from me, but only the because thou art hys wyfe. How than can I do thys great wykydnes, for to synne agaynst God?
And after thys maner spake she to Ioseph daye by day: but he harkend not vnto her, to slepe nere her, or to be in her company.
And it fortuned aboute the same season, that Ioseph entred in to the house, to do hys busynes: & there was none of the housholde by, in the house.
And she caught hym by the garment saying: come slepe wyth me. And he left his garment in her hande & fled and got him out.
When she sawe that he had left hys garment in her hande, and was fled out,
she called vnto the men of the house, & tolde them sayinge: Se, he hath brought in an Hebrewe vnto vs to do vs shame: for he came in to me, for to haue slept wyth me. But I cryed with a loude voyce.
And when he harde, that I lyfte vp my voyce & cryed, he left hys garment wt me & fled away and got him out.
And she layed vp his garment by her, vntil her Lord came home.
And she told him accordyng to these wordes saying. This Hebrues seruaunte whiche thou hast brought vnto vs came in to me to do me shame.
But as soone as I lyft vp my voyce and cryed, he left hys garment with me & fled out.
When his master herde the woordes of his wyfe which she told hym sayinge: after thys maner dyd thy seruaunte to me, he waxed wrooth.
And he toke Ioseph & put him in preson: euen in the place where the kinges prisoners laye bounde. And there continued he in preson,
but the Lorde was wyth Ioseph & shewed hym mercye, & got him fauoure in the syghte of the keper of the preso
which commytted to Iosephs hande all the presoners that were in the preson house. And what soeuer was done there, that dyd he.
And the keper of the preson loked vnto nothynge that was vnder hys hande, because the Lorde was wyth hym, and because that what soeuer he dyd, the Lorde made it come luckely to passe.
40: And it chaunced after this, that the chefe butlar of the kyng of Egypte and hys chefe baker had offended their Lorde the kynge of Egipte.
And Pharao was angrye wt them and put them inwarde in hys chefe marshals house:
euen in the preson where Ioseph was bound.
And the chefe marshall gaue Ioseph a charge wyth them, and he serued them. And they contynued a season inwarde.

And they dreamed ether of them in one nyghte: both the butlar and the baker of the kynge of Egypte whych were bounde in the preson house, ether of them hys dreame, and eche mannes dreame of a sondrye interpretacion.
When Ioseph came in vnto them in the mornyng, & loked vpon them: beholde, they were sadd. And he asked them saying:
wherfore loke ye so sadly to day?
They answered him, we haue dreamed a dreame, & haue no man to declare it. And Ioseph sayd vnto them. Interpretynge belongeth to God but tell me yet.
And the chefe butlar tolde his dreame to Ioseph and sayde vnto hym. In my dreame me thought there stode a vyne before me,
& in the vyne were .iij. braunches, and it was as though it budded, and her blossoms shott forth: & the grapes there of waxed rype.
And I had Pharaos cuppe in my hand, and toke of the grapes & wronge them into Pharaos cuppe, & delyuered Pharaos cuppe in to hys hande.
And Ioseph sayd vnto him, this is the interpretacion of it.

The .iij. braunches are thre dayes: for wythin thre dayes shall Pharao lyft vp thyne heade, & restore the vnto thyne offyce agayne, and thou shalt delyuer Pharaos cuppe in to his hande, after the old maner, euen as thou dydest when thou wast his butlar.
But thynke on me wyth the, when thou art in good case, and shewe mercy vnto me. And make mencion of me to Pharao, & helpe to brynge me oute of thys house:
for I was stollen out of the lande of the Hebrues, & here also haue I done nothing at all wherfore they should haue put me in to thys dongeon.
When the chefe baker sawe that he had well interpretate it, he sayde vnto Ioseph, me thought also in my dreame, that I had .iij. wyker baskettes on my heade.
And in the vppermost basket of all maner bakemeates for Pharao. And the byrdes ate them out of the basket vpon my head.
Ioseph answered and sayde: thys is the interpretacion therof. The .iij. baskettes are .iij. dayes,
for thys daye .iij. dayes shall Pharao take thy heade from the, and shall hange the on a tree, and the byrdes shall eate thy fleshe from of the.

And it came to passe the thyrde day which was Pharaos byrth daye, that he made a feast vnto all hys seruauntes. And he lyfted vp the head of the chefe buttelar and of the chefe baker amonge his seruauntes.
And restored the chefe buttelar vnto hys buttelarshippe agayne, and he reched the cuppe in to Pharaos hande,
and hanged the chefe baker euen as Ioseph had interpretated vnto them.
Notwythstandyng the chefe buttelar remembred not Ioseph, but forgat hym.
41: And it fortuned at .ij. yeres ende that Pharao dreamed, & thought that he stode by a ryuers syde,
and that there came out of the ryuer .vij. goodly kyne and fatflesshed, and fedd in a medowe,
and hym thought that .vij. other kyne came vp after them out of the ryuer euel fauored and leane fleshed and stode by the other vpon the brynke of the ryuer.
And the euyll fauored and leans flesshed kyne: ate vp the .vij. wel fauored and fat kyne: and he awoke there wyth.
And he slepte agayne and dreamed the second tyme, that seuen eares of corne grewe vpon one stalke rancke and goodly.
And that .vij. thynne eares blasted wyth the wynde, sprange vp after them:
and that the .vij. thynne eares deuoured the .vij. rancke and full eares. And than Pharao awaked: & se, here is his dreame.

When the mornynge came, hys sprete was troubled. And he sent and called for all the sothesayers of Egypte & al the wyse men therof, and tolde them his dreame: but there was none of them that coulde interpretate it vnto Pharao.
Than spake the chefe buttelar vnto Pharao saying. I do remembre my faute thys daye.
Pharao was angrye wt his seruauntes, & put in warde in the chefe marshals house both me & the chefe baker.
And we dreamed both of vs in one nyght & ech mannes dreame of a sondrye interpretacion.
And there was wyth vs a yonge man, an Hebrue borne, seruaunte vnto the chefe marshall. And we told hym, and he declared our dreames to vs accordynge to ether of oure dreames.
And as he declared them vnto vs, euen so it came to passe. I was restored to myne office agayn, and he was hanged.
Than Pharao sent & called Ioseph. And they made him haste out of preison. And he shaued him self and chaunged his rayment, and went in to Pharao.
And Pharao sayde vnto Ioseph: I haue dreamed a dreame & no man can interpretate it, but I haue herde say of the that as sone as thou hearest a dreame thou dost interpretate it.
And Ioseph answered Pharao saying: God shal geue Pharao an answere of peace without me.
Pharao sayd vnto Ioseph: in my dreame me thought I stode by a ryuers syde,
and there cam out of the ryuer .vij. fat fleshed and well fauored kyne, and fedde in the meddow.
And then .vij. other kyne came vp after them, poore & very euell fauored & leane fleshed: so that I neuer sawe their lyke in all the lande of Egypte in euell fauordnesse.
And the .vij. leane and euel fauored kyne eate vp the fyrste .vij. fat kyne.
And when they had eaten them vp a man coulde not perceyue that they had eaten them: for they were styll as euyll fauored as they were at the begynnyng. And I awoke.
And I sawe agayn in my dreame .vij. eares spring out of one stalke ful and good,
and .vij. other eares wytherd, thynne an blasted wt wynde, sprynge vp after them.
And the thynne eares deuowred the .vij. good eares. And I haue tolde it vnto the sothsayers, but no man can tell me what it meaneth.
Then Ioseph sayde vnto Pharao: both Pharaos dreames are one. And God doth shewe Pharao what he is aboute to do.
The seuen good kyne are .vij. yeres: & the seuen good eares: are seuen yeres also, and it is but one dreame.
Likewyse the seuen thynne and euel fauored kyne that came out after them, are seuen yeres: and the .vij. emptye and blasted eares shalbe .vij. yeres of hunger.
This is that whiche I sayde vnto Pharao, that god doth shewe Pharao what he is about to do.
Beholde there shal come .vij. yere of great plenteousnes through oute all the lande of Egypte.
And there shal aryse after them .vij. yeres of hunger. So that al the plenteousnes shalbe forgotten in the lande of Egypt. And the hunger shall consume the lande:
so that the plenteousnes shall not be once a sene in the lande by reason of that hunger that shall come after, for it shalbe exceadynge greate.
And as concernynge that the dreame was doubled vnto Pharao the seconde tyme, it betokeneth that the thynges is certanly prepared of God, and that God wyll shortlye brynge it to passe.
Nowe therfore let Pharao prouyde for a man of vnderstandyng & wysdome, and set him ouer the land of Egypte.
And let Pharao make offycers ouer the lande, & take vp the fyfte parte of the lande of Egypte in the .vij. plenteous yeres
& let them gather all the foode of these good yeres that come, and lay vp corne vnder the power of Pharao, that there may be foode in the cyties,
and there let them kepe it: that there maye be foode in stoore in the lande, agaynste the .vij. yeres of hunger whych shal come in the land of Egypte, and that the land perysh not thorow hunger.
And the sayinge pleased Pharao & all his seruauntes.
Than sayde Pharao vnto hys seruauntes: where shal we fynde soch a man as thys is, that hath the sprete of GOD in hym?
wherfore Pharao sayde vnto Ioseph: for as moch as God hath shewed the al this, there is no man of vnderstandyng or of wysdome lyke vnto the.
Thou therfore shalt be ouer my house, and acordyng to thy worde shall al my people obeye: only in the kynges seate wyll I be aboue the.
And he sayde vnto Ioseph: beholde, I haue set the ouer all the lande of Egypte.
And he toke of hys rynge from hys fyngre, and put it vpon Iosephs fyngre, and arayed him in rayment of bysse, & put a golden cheyne about hys neck
& set him vpon the best charet that he had saue one. And they cryed before hym Abrech, & that Pharao had made him ruelar ouer al the land of Egypte.
And Pharao said vnto Ioseph: I am Pharao, without thy wyll, shall no man lyfte vp ether his hand or fote in al the land of Egypte.
And he called Iosephs name Zaphnath Paena. And he gaue him to wyfe Asnath the daughter of Putiphar preast of On. Than went Ioseph abrode in the lande of Egypte.
And he was .xxx. yere olde when he stode before Pharao kyng of Egypte. And than Ioseph departed from Pharao, & went thorow out al the lande of Egypte.
And in the .vij. plenteous yeres they made sheues

& gathered vp all the fode of the .vij. plenteous yeres whych were in the lande of Egypte & put it in to the cyties. And he put the foode of the feldes that grewe rounde about euery cyte: euen in the same.
And Ioseph layde vp corne in stoore, lyke vnto the sande of the sea in multitude out of mesure, vntyll he left nombrynge: For it was wyth out nombre.
And vnto Ioseph were borne .ij. sonnes before the yeres of hunger came, which Asnath the doughter of Putiphar preast of On, bare vnto him.
And he called the name of the fyrst sonne Manasse, for God (sayde he) hath made me forget all my laboure and all my fathers houshold.
The seconde called he Ephraim, for God (sayde he) hath caused me to growe in the lande of my trouble.
And when the .vij. yeres of plenteousnes that was in the land of Egypte were ended,
than came the .vij. yeres of derth, acordyng as Ioseph had sayd. And the derth was in all landes: but in the lande of Egypte was there yet foode.
When now all the lande of Egypt beganne to hunger, than cryed the people to Pharao for breade. And Pharao sayde vnto all Egypte: goo vnto Iosephe, and what he sayth to you that doo.
And when the dearthe was throw out all the lande, Ioseph opened all that was in the cyties and solde vnto the Egypcyans. And hunger waxed sore in the lande of Egypte:
And all countrees came to Egypte to Ioseph for to bye corne: bicause that the hunger was so sore in all the landes.
42: When Iacob sawe that ther was corne to be solde in Egypte, he sayd vnto hys sonnes: why are ye negligent?
beholde, I haue harde that there is corne to be solde in Egypte. Gette you thyther and by vs corne from thence, that we maye lyue and not dye.
So went Iosephs ten brethren doune to bye corne in Egypte,
for Beniamyn Iosephs brother woulde not Iacob sende wyth hys other bretheren: for he sayde: some misfortune myght happen hym.
And the sonnes of Israel came to bye corne among other that came, for there was derth also in the lande of Canaan.
And Ioseph was gouernour in the land, and solde corne to all the people of the land. And his brethren came, & fel flat on the grounde before him.
When Ioseph sawe his brethren, he knewe them: But made straung vnto them, and spake roughly vnto them sayinge: Whence come ye? & they sayde: out of the lande of Canaan, to bye vytayle.
Ioseph knewe his brethren, but they knewe not hym.
And Ioseph remembred his dreames which he dreamed of them, and sayde vnto them: ye are spies, and to se where the lande is weake is youre comynge.
And they sayd vnto hym: nay my Lorde: but to bye vytayle thy seruauntes are come.
We are al one mans sonnes, & meane truely, and thy seruauntes are no spies.
And he sayd vnto them: nay verely, but euen to se where the lande is weake is youre comyng.
And they sayde: we thy seruauntes are .xij. brethren, the sonnes of one man in the lande of Canaan. The yongest is yet with oure father, and one, no man woteth where he is.
Ioseph sayde vnto them, that is it that I sayde vnto you, that ye are surelye spies.
Here by ye shall be proued. For by the lyfe of Pharao, ye shall not go hence, vntyll your yongest brother be come hither.

Sende therfore one of you and let him fet your brother, and ye shalbe in preyson in the meane season. And thereby shall youre wordes be proued, whether there be any trueth in you: or els by the lyfe of Pharao, ye are but spies
And he put them in warde thre dayes.
And Ioseph said vnto them the thyrd day: Thys do and lyue, for I feare God.
If ye meane no hurte, let one of youre brethren be bounde in the preyson, and go ye and brynge the necessarie foode vnto youre housholdes,
and brynge youre yongest brother vnto me: that youre wordes maye be beleued, and that ye dye not. And they dyd so.
Than they sayde one to another: we haue verely synned agaynst oure brother, in that we sawe the anguysh of hys soull when he besought vs, & wold not heare him: therfore is thys troubyll come vpon vs.
Ruben answered them sayinge: sayd I not vnto you that ye shulde not synne agaynst the lad? but ye wolde not heare. And nowe verely see, hys bloud is requyred.
They were not aware that Ioseph vnderstode them, for he spake vnto them by an interpreter.
And he turned from them & wepte, and than turned to them again and comened with them, & toke out Symeon from amonge them and bounde hym before their eyes,
& commaunded to fyl their sackes wyth corne, and to put euery mans money in his sacke, and to geue them vitayle to spende by the waye. And so it was done to them.
And they laded theyr asses wyth the corne and departed thence.
And as one of them opened hys sacke, for to geue hys asse prouender in the Inne, he spyed hys money in hys sacks mouth.

And he sayde vnto hys brethren: my money is restored me agayne, and is euen in my sackes mouth. Than their hartes fayled them, and were astoynyed and sayde one to another: howe cometh it that God dealeth thus wyth vs.
And they came vnto Iacob their father vnto the land of Canaan, and tolde hym all that had happened them sayinge.
The Lorde of the lande spake roughly to vs, and toke vs for spyes to serch the countre.
And we sayde vnto hym: we meane truely and are no spyes.
We be .xij. brethren sonnes of oure father, one is away, and the yongest is now wyth oure father in the lande of Canaan.
And the Lorde of the countre sayde vnto vs: here by shal I knowe yf ye meane truely: leaue one of youre brethren here with me, and take foode necessary for youre housholdes and get you away,
and brynge youre yongest brother vnto me. And thereby shall I knowe that ye are no spyes, but meane truely: So wyll I delyuer you youre brother agayn, and ye shal occupye in the lande.
And as they emptied their sackes, behold: euery mans bundel of money was in his sacke. And when both they & their father sawe the bundels of money, they were afrayde.
And Iacob their father said vnto them: Me haue ye robbed of my chyldren: Ioseph is away, and Symeon is awaye, and ye wyll take Ben Iamin awaye. All these thynges fall vpon me.
Ruben answered hys father sayinge: Slee my two sonnes, yf I brynge him not to the agayn. Delyuer hym therfore to my hande, and I wyll brynge hym to the agayne:

And he sayde: my sonne shall not go doune wyth you. For his brother is dead, & he is left alone. Moreouer some mysfortune myght happen vpon him by the way whych ye go. And so shuld ye bring my gray head with sorowe vnto the graue.
43: And the derth waxed sore in the lande.
And when they had eaten vp the corne which they brought out of the lande of Egypt, their father sayde vnto them: go agayn and by vs a lytle food.
Than sayd Iuda vnto him: the man dyd testifye vnto vs sayinge loke that ye sea not my face excepte your brother be wyth you.
Therfore yf thou wylt sende oure brother wyth vs, we wyl go and bye the food.
